title: Two Panels
youtube_title: Charges filed. She engraves the first two panels of evidence
logline: The prosecutor's office files the pickup log and the examiner's report, and Nora engraves the first two panels for her twelve-slot evidence wall; Peg stands at the wall a long time, with a slip of paper in her hand.
hook: The prosecutor's filing receipt clips onto the light box: two exhibits, the pickup log and the examiner's report. She tapes a note that says “Left hand” beside the rack and picks up the engraving pen.
mid_hook: The pen moves stroke by stroke: “Pills: pharmacy pickup log.” “Signature: examiner's report.” The two panels slide into the first two of twelve slots, and Number Three's fire throws the words onto the brick.
extra_hooks: Sparks counts them. “Two down!” “Ten to go!” Peg doesn't look up. “Good at math, aren't you.”
conflict: The wall finally has something on it, but only two of twelve slots. Whose left hand traced her name? She won't chase it or confront anyone; she hands it to the prosecutor. And Peg stands at the wall and won't leave.
turn: You think two engraved panels are the end of the day. The real thing happens after everyone leaves: alone in front of them, Peg tears open the cover of her ledger.

cliffhanger.text: Late night, only the furnace glow. Peg is still at the wall. From a slit in the ledger's cover she pulls a tiny folded slip and holds it a long time. She turns. “Nora.” “The third panel.” “What goes on it?”
cliffhanger.question: Will Peg hand over that slip?

spectacle: Two engraved panels slot into the first two places on the twelve-slot steel rack; Number Three's firelight passes through the letters and throws “Pills” and “Signature” across the red brick wall.
glamour_shot: She bends over the glass with the engraving pen, goggles pushed up on her head, sleeves rolled; with every stroke the furnace light jumps on her lashes.
general_payoffs: The first two panels go up on the evidence wall: “Pills: pharmacy pickup log” and “Signature: examiner's report”
The left-hand lead goes to the prosecutor; she doesn't go after Sienna on her own

title: I Was One Day Late
youtube_title: Peg finally hands over a receipt, and what her son said
logline: At the evidence wall, Peg tells what she has hidden for two months: the receipt in her son's car, the phone call that night, and her own night in the same hallway thirty-four years ago.
hook: Peg flattens the slip on the light box. A receipt from a confectionery that makes prop candy. Item: “Replica tablets.” Qty: “100.” In the corner, a number: 0417-100. “The day you left the hospital.” “It was in his car.”
mid_hook: “That night,” “he slept at my place.” “Out on the porch, on the phone.” “I heard him say,” “That thing's taken care of.”
extra_hooks: She takes off her reading glasses. “Thirty-four years ago,” “I sat in that same hallway.” “All night.” “His father never came.”
conflict: Hand this over and she is a mother testifying against her own son. She has kept it two months, watching her daughter-in-law dig and hold on alone.
turn: You think Peg kept quiet to protect her son. She kept quiet because she already knew, and couldn't admit the boy she raised could do it. She left with Nora because thirty-four years ago, nobody left with her.

cliffhanger.text: Peg pushes the receipt across the table. “I'm not helping you.” “I'm helping that baby.” A long pause. “I was one day late.” Nora stands and hugs her, for the first time. Peg goes stiff, then lifts a hand and pats her back once.
cliffhanger.question: Can this receipt sink him?

spectacle: The light box shines up through a crumpled receipt; “Replica tablets”, “100” and the number in the corner glow as if they were etched in glass.
glamour_shot: The moment she hugs Peg, her shoulder-length hair against Peg's worn cardigan, the furnace lights them from behind and their two shadows merge into one.
general_payoffs: Why Peg left with her is revealed: the day Nora left the hospital, Peg found a receipt in Grant's car from a confectionery that makes prop candy, “Replica tablets, 100 count”, and that night heard him on the phone: “That thing's taken care of.” Thirty-four years ago she sat alone all night in the same Merrow General hallway

title: No Name, Not Enough
youtube_title: She takes Peg's receipt to the prosecutor. He asks one thing
logline: Nora takes Peg and the receipt to the prosecutor's office; Reyes sees what the paper is worth but says without the buyer's name it isn't enough, and tells her Grant's lawyer came by today.
hook: The prosecutor's office. Reyes holds the receipt under his desk lamp a long time. “Who placed the order?” “No name,” “it's not enough.”
mid_hook: Peg takes the receipt back off his desk, folds it and tucks it into the ledger cover. “Then I keep it.” “Till there's a name.”
extra_hooks: In the corridor Peg slows down. Quietly: “When he broke a dish as a boy,” “he did this too.” “Hid it first.”
conflict: The receipt proves someone bought a hundred replica tablets, not who ordered them. She can't go question the confectionery herself; she can only wait for the prosecutor to dig.
turn: She thinks she has been turned away again, but Reyes's last line shows her the board: Grant is scared. The moment the forgery charge was filed, his lawyer came asking if she'd drop the case.

cliffhanger.text: As they stand to go, Reyes closes the file without looking up. “Oh. One thing.” “His lawyer” “came by today.” “Asked if you'd drop the case.”
cliffhanger.question: Why is Grant rushing her?

spectacle: Under the desk lamp in the prosecutor's office, a crumpled receipt lies on a thick case file; the light stops exactly on the blank “Ordered by” line.
glamour_shot: She walks Peg down the long corridor of the prosecutor's office, shoulder-length hair, dark coat, the fluorescent lights sliding back over their heads; her step is steadier than Peg's.
general_payoffs: Reyes has seen the receipt: someone ordered a hundred replica tablets
She sees Grant is scared: his lawyer came asking whether she'll drop the case
locations: Merrow County Prosecutor's Office (Reyes's office, corridor)

title: Number Three Can't Go Cold
youtube_title: The ferry night moves up, and the old furnace man goes down
logline: The ferry terminal moves its maiden voyage up a week with twelve blue panels still unblown; that same night Gus throws out his back hauling cullet alone, and Number Three can't be allowed to go cold.
hook: Fiona stands in Remelt's doorway with the spec binder. “The maiden voyage” “moved up to next Friday.” Sparks looks at the half-built chandelier on the rack. “We've still got twelve…”
mid_hook: Midnight. Gus hauls a sack of cullet alone, locks up halfway bent, and eases himself down to the floor against the furnace. “My back.”
extra_hooks: She calls a car to take him to a doctor; Gus grabs her sleeve and won't go. “The furnace.” “Can't go cold.” “It goes cold,” “the brick cracks.”
conflict: Twelve panels in eight days. If Number Three goes cold, its twelve-year-old brick could crack through. Only Gus knows how to tend it, and she still can't go near a hot furnace.
turn: She thought the deadline was the hard part. It's people: the only blower is a twenty-year-old apprentice, the man who keeps the fire is down, and she can't touch the furnace.

cliffhanger.text: Gus on the floor, gripping her sleeve. “If I go,” “who watches the fire” “tonight?” Number Three roars on. The clock on the wall hits ten.
cliffhanger.question: Who keeps Number Three lit?

spectacle: In Number Three's firelight a sack of cullet spills across the floor, blue and clear shards everywhere, reflecting an old man sitting on the ground.
glamour_shot: She crouches beside Gus with a hand on his back, her apron dusted white, and looks back at the roaring furnace; for the first time her eyes show a flicker of panic.
general_payoffs: She gets Gus onto the cot and has a doctor come to the shop

title: The Man in the Heat Gloves
youtube_title: Who watches the furnace? Her contract husband walks in
logline: With no one to tend Number Three, Elias shows up at night in heat gloves; he tends the fire and never touches her chandelier while Nora calls the moves and Sparks blows panel after panel, seven nights straight.
hook: Ten p.m. The steel door swings open: Elias in work clothes, thick heat gloves on both hands. “Gus called me.” Gus lifts a hand from the cot. “Mr. Ashford.” “The fire's yours.”
mid_hook: “You know how?” He shovels cullet into the furnace mouth. “Gus taught me.” Then he turns back to the furnace, his back to her, and says nothing more.
extra_hooks: 2 a.m. Theo sneaks in with takeout, typing on his tablet. “Mrs. Ashford Observation Log.” “2 a.m.” “Boss is stoking a furnace.”
conflict: She has to finish twelve panels and can't let Elias touch her chandelier: clause two. Tending the fire is the landlord's furnace and a favor for Gus; which panel gets blown, and how, belongs to her and Sparks.
turn: She expects him to pitch in on the rush. For seven nights he does exactly one thing: the fire. The chandelier is hers, the furnace is his, and he doesn't cross that line by an inch.

cliffhanger.text: Dawn on the seventh day, twenty-three blue panels on the rack. She hands Sparks the blowpipe. “Last one.” “All yours.” “I won't call it.” Sparks's grip on the pipe shakes.
cliffhanger.question: Can Sparks do it without her?

spectacle: Remelt at night: a gloved figure feeds the furnace mouth shovel by shovel, and the firelight throws his shadow across the whole evidence wall, over the two engraved panels.
glamour_shot: Elias, work sleeves rolled to the forearm, pushes the furnace door shut in thick gloves; his thin-framed glasses catch the fire and sweat runs down his temple. He doesn't look back.
general_payoffs: Number Three never goes cold: Elias tends it seven nights straight
The chandelier reaches twenty-three panels

title: Straight: 1
youtube_title: 24 crooked tries later, he blows the last panel alone
logline: Sparks blows the last blue panel on his own and it comes out straight; all twenty-four panels are done, but one call from the ferry terminal adds a guest to the maiden voyage.
hook: Arms folded behind the safety line, she says nothing. Sparks gathers, turns, blows; Gus watches, propped up on the cot. The glass comes out. Three seconds of silence. Sparks: “…It's straight?” Nora: “It's straight.”
mid_hook: Sparks grabs the chalk and, next to “Crooked: 24” on the wall, starts a new column: “Straight: 1.” Gus laughs out loud on the cot, then grabs his side. “Ow—” “My back.”
extra_hooks: Before dawn the twenty-four blue panels go into wooden crates one by one. By the furnace there's only a pair of heat gloves on the floor. Elias is already gone.
conflict: If the last panel comes out crooked, they miss tomorrow night's maiden voyage. She has to keep her mouth shut and let Sparks stand up there alone.
turn: She thought she wouldn't be able to stay quiet, and she never makes a sound. His first straight piece is what she taught him, and it's his own.

cliffhanger.text: Fiona calls. “The maiden voyage sponsor” “is Whitlock Home.” “Mr. Whitlock” “is giving a speech.” She looks at the twenty-four crates and says nothing.
cliffhanger.question: Grant on her big night?

spectacle: Remelt before dawn: twenty-four panels of early-morning harbor blue lined up on the wooden rack; the first daylight comes through the high windows and all twenty-four light up at once.
glamour_shot: She stands behind the safety line with her arms folded, goggles up on her head, biting her lip as Sparks blows the last panel; when the glass comes out, her eyes smile first.
general_payoffs: Sparks blows his first straight piece
All twenty-four ferry chandelier panels are done in time for the maiden voyage

title: The Court Will Give It Back
youtube_title: Her chandelier lights the terminal. Then her ex calls
logline: Maiden voyage night: twenty-four blue panels light up the terminal and the blind-review envelope says “Remelt”; onstage Grant can only say congratulations, and afterward he calls with an offer.
hook: The terminal hall goes dark, and twenty-four blue panels light up at once, hanging like dawn waves rolling in over the harbor. The whole room looks up. Nobody says a word.
mid_hook: Fiona takes the stage. “It was a blind review.” “We only learned who” “when we opened the envelope.” “Remelt.” Every head turns to find the designer; she's at the very back in her work jacket.
extra_hooks: Sponsor's remarks. Grant has just said “supporting local design” when a reporter calls out: “The designer's your ex-wife.” “Any thoughts?” His smile stalls a beat. “…Congratulations to her.”
Before the crowd leaves, she presses a wedding ring into Peg's palm. “The first ferry check.” “I got it back.” Peg grumbles, “Who asked you to?” and puts it on right there.
conflict: It's her first work hung in a public space, and Grant is the sponsor: he means to stand under her light and talk up his brand.
turn: Grant thinks the sponsor's podium lets him make the chandelier his. Once the blind-review envelope is opened, the whole room knows who made it, and all he can say on camera is “Congratulations.”

cliffhanger.text: In the car home, her phone rings. Grant. “Drop the case” “and you get the house back.” “I don't need you to give it back.” “The court will.” She hangs up. The screen lights again, a text: “Then I'll come to you.” “Face to face.”
cliffhanger.question: Is he coming to her door?

spectacle: The three-story ferry terminal hall: twenty-four blue panels light up together and wash the whole space in harbor-dawn blue, while outside the glass wall a ferry sounds its horn and docks.
glamour_shot: She stands in the back row looking up at her own light, work jacket, shoulder-length hair, blue light all over her face; she doesn't smile, but her eyes shine like glass.
general_payoffs: The ferry terminal chandelier lights up; the blind-review envelope reads “Remelt”
With the first ferry payment she buys back Peg's wedding ring
She turns Grant down: she won't drop the case, and the court will give the house back

title: As Long as It's Lit
youtube_title: Her ex wants a meeting. She picks the place: her own studio
logline: Nora sets the meeting at Remelt; Dana warns Elias he can't fight her battles, he says he's only tending the furnace, and that night at the fire he says something that doesn't sound like a contract.
hook: She texts back: “Remelt.” “Tomorrow, eight p.m.” On the phone Dana's voice jumps. “What are you negotiating?” “I'm not.” “I'm letting him look.”
mid_hook: Top floor of Ashford Construction. Dana slaps a file on the desk. “You can't fight for her.” Elias doesn't look up. “I won't.” “Gus is still laid up.” “I tend the furnace.” Theo quietly logs it: “Boss.” “Furnace.”
extra_hooks: The living room of the Ashford house. Peg's needles go faster and faster. “I'm coming too.” “Mom.” “You stay home.” Peg sets the needles down. “Then you come home” “and eat your stew.”
conflict: Grant is coming to her place to bargain. She won't let anyone speak for her, but she knows that tomorrow night it won't be just the two of them in that shop.
turn: She expects Elias to keep his distance under clause two. He says he'll be there: not beside her, at the furnace. It's his furnace. He'd be there anyway.

cliffhanger.text: Late night, only the furnace light. Elias, in heat gloves, feeds the furnace mouth. She sets a bowl of pasta on the steel stool beside him; without looking he says, “Salty.” She laughs. “Tomorrow,” “you'll be here?” Eyes on the fire: “As long as it's lit,” “I'm here.”
cliffhanger.question: Will he only tend the fire?

spectacle: Remelt late at night, Number Three's fire the only light; steam off a bowl of pasta and the heat from the furnace mouth twist together in the air, and the two engraved panels flicker bright and dark.
glamour_shot: Elias at the furnace mouth, black work clothes, heat gloves, the fire turning his profile orange; when he says “As long as it's lit, I'm here,” his eyes behind the lenses aren't on her.
general_payoffs: She sets the meeting in her own studio and lets the evidence wall do the talking

title: He Walks In
youtube_title: Her ex's car turns onto Kiln Row. She leaves the door open
logline: Grant's car turns onto Kiln Row; Nora teaches Sparks the wrist turn with an empty blowpipe while Elias keeps the furnace with his back to the door. She doesn't shut the steel door.
hook: 7:58 p.m. Her phone lights up. Theo: “His car” “just turned onto Kiln Row.”
mid_hook: The engine dies outside. Dress shoes on gravel, step by step. Sparks, low: “Should I” “shut the door?” “Let him in.” “Let him look.”
extra_hooks: Dr. Brandt's ban still holds, so her blowpipe is empty; she's only teaching Sparks the wrist turn. “Wrist.” “Don't stop.” At the furnace mouth, Elias, gloved, back to the door, shovels in cullet.
conflict: She'll face him on her own ground: no shouting, no begging, no one speaking for her. All she has is a wall with two panels and an empty blowpipe.
turn: You expect her to shut the door and hide behind someone. She leaves it open and keeps teaching Sparks the wrist turn. What she wants him to see first isn't the evidence. It's her, back at the furnace.

cliffhanger.text: The footsteps stop outside. The steel door creaks open a crack, and a hand with a glass cufflink rests on it: streetlight on one side, furnace glow on the other.
cliffhanger.question: What does he want inside?

spectacle: Remelt's steel door swings slowly open; the Kiln Row streetlight outside and Number Three's fire inside meet at the threshold, where a man in a pale suit stands on the line.
glamour_shot: She holds a cold blowpipe between the furnace and the door, shoulder-length hair, work apron, goggles pushed up; when the door creaks she doesn't turn around, and her wrist keeps turning.
general_payoffs: She doesn't shut the door; she waits for him on her own ground
Grant comes in person; his car stops outside Remelt

title: Hello, Sales. Twelve Years.
youtube_title: Her ex mocks two panels. Then the man at the furnace turns
logline: Grant looks at two panels of glass, tells Nora to drop the case and says she can't beat him alone; he never sees it coming when the figure at the furnace turns around and brings back his name from twelve years ago.
hook: Grant's first time inside Remelt. He takes in the brick, the bead stopped at Charges, stops at the evidence wall, taps the first panel with his glass cufflink and smiles. “Two panels of glass.” “Drop it, Nor.” “You can't beat me alone.”
mid_hook: He steps closer, voice soft. “You think Elias” “is helping you” “out of kindness?” Her blowpipe keeps turning. “I know.” “I'm using him too.”
extra_hooks: She looks at the twelve slots. “Twelve.” “The day they're full,” “you get sentenced.” He laughs. “Twelve?” “You don't even have a third.”
conflict: Grant wants the case dropped tonight. He has lawyers, money and the press; she has two panels of glass. She has to show him she won't drop it and isn't afraid, without knowing what lies between him and the man at the furnace.
turn: Grant thinks he came to tidy up an ex-wife. He needles her, laughs at her two panels, and never once notices the figure at the furnace until that man turns around.

cliffhanger.text: At the furnace, Elias turns and pulls off his heat glove: an old burn scar across the back of his left hand. Grant's smile freezes. “…You.” Elias: “Hello, Sales.” “Twelve years.” Nora's blowpipe stops mid-air. Only people from Pell's ever called him that.
cliffhanger.question: Who was Elias at Pell's?

spectacle: Number Three's fire pours out of the furnace mouth onto a left hand just stripped of its heat glove, an old burn scar across the back; behind it, on the red brick, the two engraved panels catch the same fire.
glamour_shot: Elias turns at the fire and pulls off the heat glove finger by finger; under the rolled cuff the old scar on the back of his left hand shows, and his eyes behind the lenses are locked on Grant.
general_payoffs: Grant sets foot in Remelt for the first time and sees the two panels
She refuses to his face: when the twelve slots are full, he gets sentenced
Grant recognizes Elias and, for the first time in front of her, stops smiling
Elias's left hand isn't hidden anymore: an old burn scar across the back
locations: Remelt Studio (evidence wall, Furnace No. 3 furnace mouth)
